investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing the eval from creating a new remote agent and collecting any required evidence. All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the identical failure message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step before any downstream VM readiness or runtime logic is reached.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning a 409 Conflict with error code "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents request issued by the eval runner. Because the eval probe calls createAgent() as its very first substantive step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), the 409 causes an immediate failure before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) can be collected. The quota condition is the earliest violated contract boundary: the API rejects agent creation entirely, so no subsequent VM readiness or runtime assertions can be evaluated. This is an eval-observed failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to end users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1330 — well under the warningLatencyMs of 240000, confirming the probe failed fast on the 409 rather than timing out
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm agent quota at the org or account level used by the eval runner has reached its hard limit of 100. The 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', and the same error is returned for all three independent check invocations, indicating the quota is exhausted before any new agent can be created.

Secondary — A previous eval run (or runs) created remote agents that were not cleaned up, consuming quota slots. The runner uses withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1857) to track and delete resources, but if a prior run crashed or the cleanup path was not reached, orphaned agents may be holding quota.
Tertiary — The eval runner's probe account or org is shared with other workloads that independently consumed quota, leaving no headroom for the observability probes.

Lower confidence — A quota limit configuration change on the swarm backend reduced the per-org cap to a value already exceeded by existing agents; no source evidence in this packet supports this directly.

Because the remote-agent-state probe calls createAgent as its first substantive action (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1879), the 409 caused an immediate failure before any evidence could be written, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing. The same 409 body was returned to all three sibling checks, confirming the quota condition is the single shared upstream blocker rather than a per-check code defect.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is being rejected with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing the eval from creating a new remote agent and collecting any required evidence. All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the identical failure message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step before any downstream VM readiness or runtime logic is reached.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning a 409 Conflict with error code "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents request issued by the eval runner. Because the eval probe calls createAgent() as its very first substantive step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), the 409 causes an immediate failure before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) can be collected. The quota condition is the earliest violated contract boundary: the API rejects agent creation entirely, so no subsequent VM readiness or runtime assertions can be evaluated. This is an eval-observed failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to end users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm agent quota at the org or account level used by the eval runner has reached its hard limit of 100. The 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', and the same error is returned for all three independent check invocations, indicating the quota is exhausted before any new agent can be created.

Secondary — A previous eval run (or runs) created remote agents that were not cleaned up, consuming quota slots. The runner uses withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1857) to track and delete resources, but if a prior run crashed or the cleanup path was not reached, orphaned agents may be holding quota.
Tertiary — The eval runner's probe account or org is shared with other workloads that independently consumed quota, leaving no headroom for the observability probes.

Lower confidence — A quota limit configuration change on the swarm backend reduced the per-org cap to a value already exceeded by existing agents; no source evidence in this packet supports this directly.
